newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila rates steady as traders await next auction.
newsitem.headline: Manila rates steady as traders await next auction.

text.p: Philippine treasury bill rates in the secondary market were steady as traders opted to wait and watch if the decline in the auction rates would be sustained, traders said.
"Instead of moving down with the auction rates, some banks are cautious in quoting their bid-offer rates because they think the rates may have hit the bottom," one trader said.
T-bill rates fell on Monday due to excess liquidity, with all the rates in the 10 percent range.
"The yield curve is too flat. We may either see the one-year rate move up or 91-day rate go down to single digit," he said.
However, he said, a single-digit three-month rate might trigger an outflow of foreign funds from the fixed-income instruments due to the narrowing premium over U.S. Treasury bills.
"It will be interesting to see how the Central Bank will act on this situation," he added.
The Central Bank had kept its overnight and term rates unchanged on Wednesday.
A survey of eight banks showed that some banks are still bidding for the one-year bills at higher than 11 percent even though the auction rate had fallen to 10.917 percent on Monday.
The overnight money was unchanged at 14.03125 percent with done rates ranging from 14.03125 to 14.25 percent.
Turnover was moderate at 12.698 billion pesos.
The interbank call loan and bill markets will be closed on Thursday for independence day. They will reopen on Friday.
